71189542.text: The alternate explanation says “each of these 38 tents” after calculating a 38-person capacity deficit. The correct calculation immediately following it divides 38 by 2 to obtain 19 two-person tents. The answer C and the main elimination solution are correct.
71189542.entry: Read the deficit as 38 people. Each replacement of a four-person tent by a two-person tent removes two places, so 38/2=19 tents.

64c85440.title: The intended parking interval assumes the curb is fully allocated
64c85440.text: The official solution obtains 15 through 18 spaces by dividing the 135-foot curb by the permitted widths 9 through 7.5 feet. The lower bound 15 uses an implicit full-use assumption: if unused curb were allowed, fewer than 15 spaces could also be placed. Read D under the intended full-curb layout.
64c85440.entry: For a layout allocating all 135 feet to n equal-width standard spaces, 7.5<=135/n<=9 gives 15<=n<=18, with integer n.

daad7c32.title: The reverse spring rate is not the variable w
daad7c32.text: The original rationale correctly selects D: the spring length increases 2 centimeters per newton. Its explanation of distractor C says this describes the value w. In fact C describes the reverse rate, the increase in weight per centimeter, which is 1/2 newton per centimeter. The variable w is the weight itself. The answer D is unchanged.
daad7c32.entry: For L=30+2w, delta L/delta w=2 cm/N. Solving w=(L-30)/2 gives delta w/delta L=1/2 N/cm.

a1fd2304.title: The mixture equation conserves salt, not total solution volume
a1fd2304.text: The original rationale calls volume times concentration the total amount of saline solution. Those products measure the salt contribution; total solution volume is x+3 liters. The subsequent salt-balance equation and answer 1.5 liters are correct.
a1fd2304.entry: Use 0.10(3)+0.25x=0.15(3+x). For x=1.5, salt contributions sum to0.675, equal to0.15(4.5); the mixture volume is4.5 liters.

81b664bc.title: Use parallel intercepts; the adjacent trapezoids need not be similar
81b664bc.text: The original PDF rationale says AFEB and BEDC are similar because AF, BE, and CD are parallel. Parallel bases alone do not establish similarity of these quadrilaterals. The stated ratio and answer 17.5 are valid by the parallel intercept theorem applied to transversals AC and FD.
81b664bc.entry: The three parallel segments cut proportional consecutive lengths on the two transversals: AB/BC=FE/ED. Thus ED=18.5*8.5/9=17.4722..., which rounds to 17.5. No trapezoid similarity is required.

7268586c.title: The known angles add to 156, not 152
7268586c.text: The original rationale changes x+132+24=180 to x+152=180 and then reports x=24. The intermediate sum should be 156. The answer D, 24, and the alternate isosceles base-angle proof are correct.
7268586c.entry: Compute x=180-(132+24)=180-156=24. Alternatively PQ=QR makes the base angles P and R equal, so x=24 directly.

933fee1a.title: The right angle is C; B is the 58-degree angle
933fee1a.text: The first rationale sentence says the measure of angle B is 90 degrees while concluding that B must be 58 degrees. The diagram marks C as the right angle. Replacing B by C in the 90-degree statement restores the angle-sum argument. The selected ratio and answer B are correct.
933fee1a.entry: A=32 and C=90 imply B=58. In the other triangle D=58 and F=90 imply E=32. Matching opposite-32-degree legs and hypotenuses gives BC/AB=DF/DE.

2d31caae.title: The rejection of A describes the correct conditional percentage
2d31caae.text: The key B is correct: Employee A has16 one-star calls out of145, about11%. The rationale describes choice A as the percentage of Employee A’s calls that received one star, which is actually B’s quantity. A≈3% instead comes from16/500, using all employees’ calls. D=32% reverses the condition, using16/50. The source image is preserved.

d89c1513.title: A table column total is misprinted
d89c1513.text: The beverage cells are 60 and 35, totaling 95; the printed column total says 90. The four interior cells sum to the stated grand total of 135. The requested no-gas probability uses the unaffected row total 50/135, so key D remains correct. Use the interior cells to check inconsistent margins before choosing a denominator.

efc469c4.text: A sum of coefficients is the polynomial at 1. Match any outside scale before evaluating.

a255ae72.text: Substitute into the smallest repeated block before expanding.

77c0cced.text: One intersection means a repeated zero of the difference of the two equations.

02060533.text: Recover the requested function before reading its intercept.
02060533.entry: Multiply each table output g(x) by x+3. The recovered f values lie on f(x)=4x+36.

555939d2.text: Although filed under ratios/rates, the structure is inference from a sample. Scale8/300 to30000;800 is an estimate, not a census count.

3638f413.text: FromJanuary2001 toJanuary2005 there are four doublings. Reverse the exponential multiplier, not a linear annual increment.

3ac09984.text: Convert pesos to dollars, then retain98% after the fee on the converted amount.

8cbf1415.text: The30% striped share is conditional on being red. Multiply.4 by.3 for the joint share; this does not assume independent features.

34f8cd89.text: Multiply nested eligible shares, then subtract the whole joint event from1. “Not rectangular green metal” is not three simultaneous negative requirements.

eqx-coef: The requested sum equals 6f(1), not f(1); 6[-14*9+6*4]=-612.
eqx-rewrite: Subtract first: x²-y²=b-c; then square to b²-2bc+c².
nle-system: Subtract line from parabola: 2x²-24x+64-a has repeated root at x=6; original parabola vertex 21/4 is not the tangency x.
nle-count: b²-2704<0 and b positive integer give b<52; greatest 51.
nlf-exp: h(0)=10 gives b=9 since a>0 and a^0=1. Then a²=4 and a>0 gives a=2, so ab=18. The positive-base assumption excludes -2.

probability_review.scope: 49 question and solution OCR reviews, with ambiguous figures checked visually. These editorial groups do not predict future-test frequencies. No repeated-draw/replacement/binomial family was identified.

tm.nm: The question asks for an expression, not x: scale both sides
tl: “If 4x = 3, what is the value of 24x?”
the asked expression is a multiple, part or reciprocal of one side
tm.ask: the value of an expression such as 24x, x − 7 or 8/x
tm.rl: Multiply or divide both sides by what turns the given side into the asked one.
hd: Compare the asked expression with one side: 24x = 6 × 4x.
Do the same to the other side: 6 × 3 = 18.
For a reciprocal, flip both sides.
tr: Answering x itself
Scaling only one side

tm.nm: Solve a linear equation
tl: “what value of x is the solution”
one equation, one variable; maybe brackets, fractions or decimals
tm.ask: the solution
tm.rl: Hand for clean numbers; Desmos for decimals (type the equation, read the vertical line x = …).
ds: 0.8t-0.46=8(t-0.001)+1.9 typed with x for t: Desmos draws x = −0.3267
hd: Distribute, collect x-terms on one side, numbers on the other.
Divide by the coefficient.
tr: Sign slip when distributing a negative
Adding where subtraction is needed (w + 7 = 357 → 364)

tm.nm: Treat the repeated bracket as one unknown
tl: the same bracket appears twice, or the question asks for the bracket (2 − 4x)
tm.ask: the bracket’s value (or x through it)
tm.rl: Call the bracket u and solve for u; a bracket over two different denominators must be 0.
hd: Replace the bracket with u: 5 − 7u = 16 − 8u.
Solve for u; if x is asked, finish from u.
u/3 = u/13 forces u = 0.
tr: Expanding and solving for x, then answering x
Expecting a nonzero bracket in u/3 = u/13

tm.nm: Which equation has the same solution?
tl: “which of the following is equivalent to 4x + 6 = 12”
choices are scaled or shifted versions
tm.ask: the equivalent equation
tm.rl: Look for every term divided (or multiplied) by the same number.
hd: Divide every term by a common factor (4x + 6 = 12 → 2x + 3 = 6).
Or solve each and compare (x = 1.5).
tr: Dividing only some terms

tm.nm: How many solutions? (numbers only)
tl: “How many solutions does the given equation have?”
no unknown constants
choices: zero, exactly one, exactly two, infinitely many
tm.ask: the number of solutions
tm.rl: Simplify both sides to ax + b: same a and b → infinitely many; same a, different b → zero; different a → exactly one.
ds: Graph y=left and y=right: one crossing, parallel lines, or the same line
hd: Expand both sides.
Compare the x-coefficients first, then the constants.
tr: “Zero” for −49x = −98x (x = 0 is one solution)
“Exactly two” (never possible for a linear equation)

tm.nm: Find the constant for no solution, infinitely many, or exactly one
tl: “a is a constant”
“no solution”, “infinitely many solutions”, “exactly one solution”
tm.ask: the constant(s) or the impossible value
tm.rl: No solution: x-coefficients equal, constants different. Infinitely many: both equal. Exactly one: x-coefficients different.
ds: Slider for the constant: drag until the two lines coincide (infinitely many) or are parallel (no solution)
hd: Expand both sides into ax + b form.
Set the x-coefficients equal and solve for the constant.
For infinitely many, also set the constants equal; for “one solution”, the excluded value makes the coefficients equal.
tr: Solving for x
Matching constants when only the x-coefficients must match

tm.nm: Story: solve for the unknown amount
tl: a starting amount, a rate per unit and a target total
or a total split into known and equal parts
tm.ask: a count, time, rate or starting value
tm.rl: Write start + rate × n = total, then solve.
hd: Name the unknown; write one equation from the story.
Find a rate from two values if needed: (24,000 − 19,350) ÷ 5.
Solve and check the question asks for that quantity (total hours, not extra hours).
tr: Answering the extra time instead of the total
Using the rate itself as the answer
Forgetting the fixed fee

tm.nm: Write the equation for a story
tl: “which equation represents this situation”
a fixed part plus a per-unit part, or categories counted as n, 5n and 22
tm.ask: the equation
tm.rl: Build each part in words first; “after the first 3 hours” means (t − 3).
hd: Fixed amount + rate × (number of units the rate applies to) = total.
Chain unit rates so units cancel (dollars per mile = 4/25).
tr: Multiplying the fixed amount by the variable
Forgetting the n itself (5n + 22 instead of 6n + 22)
Inverting a unit rate (25/4)

tm.nm: Write the expression for a story
tl: “which expression represents …”
a phrase like “3 more than twice …” or x stations of one kind and the rest of another
tm.ask: the expression
tm.rl: Translate phrase by phrase; plug in a number to check.
hd: “3 more than twice n” → 2n + 3.
Two kinds: 6x + 4(5 − x) = 2x + 20.
Check with a small number.
tr: Reversing order in “more than”
Forgetting the other kind

tm.nm: What does this number mean in context?
tl: an equation in context (13,000 = 2,800 + 200t)
“best interpretation of 200” or “of 2.00x”
tm.ask: the meaning of a coefficient or a term
tm.rl: A coefficient is per one unit; a term like 2.00x is a total for x units.
hd: Coefficient of t: the amount for each one unit of t.
Product term: the total for all x units.
tr: Calling a total “per unit”

tm.nm: Evaluate f(k) (or a combination of values)
tl: f(x) given
“what is the value of f(5)”, “4f(2) − g(2)”, “f(9) − f(1)”
mostly Easy
tm.ask: a function value or a combination
tm.rl: Substitute; in Desmos define f(x) and type the combination.
hd: Replace x with the number, in brackets.
For f(p) − f(q), it is the slope × (p − q).
tr: Evaluating at the wrong input
Multiplying only part of f(2) by 4

tm.nm: Find the input that gives an output
tl: “for what value of x is g(x) = 54”
a formula in context with the output given
tm.ask: the input
tm.rl: Set the function equal to the output and solve.
ds: y=9(x-273.15)/5+32 | y=467.33 | click the intersection
hd: Write f(x) = given value.
Undo the operations in reverse order.
tr: Plugging the output in as x

tm.nm: Find a constant from one known value
tl: f(x) = mx + b with one unknown constant
one value given: f(0) = 45, j(12) = 18, g(c + 7) = c/4
tm.ask: the constant, or another value after finding it
tm.rl: Substitute the known pair, solve for the constant, then use the finished function.
hd: Put the known x and f(x) into the formula.
Solve for the constant.
If another value is asked, evaluate the completed function.
tr: Stopping at the constant when f(10) is asked

tm.nm: Write the linear model for a story
tl: a starting amount and a constant change per unit
“which equation/function models …”
tm.ask: the equation
tm.rl: y = start + rate × x (rate negative for a decrease; “1 per 550” is x/550).
hd: Starting amount is the constant.
Change per unit is the coefficient; decrease → minus.
Repeated work (paint twice) multiplies the amount.
tr: Rate and start swapped
Using 550x instead of x/550
Forgetting the second coat

tm.nm: First k units at one price, then a rate: use (x − k)
tl: “173 miles in the first 3 hours … 53 mph for the remainder”
“first session free, second half off”
x > 3 or x ≥ 2 stated
tm.ask: the function of the total x
tm.rl: Total = fixed part + rate × (x − k); simplify only if the choices are simplified.
ds: Check a choice: put x = 5 into each and compare with the story’s total
hd: Write fixed part + rate × (x − k).
Expand if the choices are in y = mx + b form (53(x − 3) + 173 = 53x + 14).
Test x = k + 1 against the story.
tr: Adding the rate to all x units (53x + 173)
Using (x − 1) when two units are special

tm.nm: Use the story: start + rate × units
tl: a starting value and a rate in words
“how much after 4 weeks”, “pressure at 105 feet”
tm.ask: the total at a given input, or the rate
tm.rl: Total = start + rate × units.
hd: Start + rate × number of units.
For a rate: (total − start) ÷ units.
tr: Leaving out the starting amount

tm.nm: Line through two given points (or two values)
tl: two (input, output) pairs in words or as h(28) = 15, h(26) = 22
“which equation defines …”, “what is the demand when …”
tm.ask: the equation, the intercept, or a predicted value
tm.rl: Slope from the two pairs, then b; Desmos regression on the two points gives both.
hd: Slope = (change in output) ÷ (change in input).
b = output − slope × input.
Years: let t = years after the start year.
tr: Slope upside down
Using the calendar year as t
Wrong sign for a decrease

tm.nm: Linear function from a table
tl: a table of x and f(x)
“which defines f”, “value of b”, “f(3)”, “x-intercept”, “h(x) = f(x) − 13”
tm.ask: the equation, a constant, a value or an intercept
tm.rl: Slope from two rows; b is the value at x = 0 (step back to it); Desmos regression does both.
ds: Table x_1, y_1 | y_1~mx_1+b
hd: Slope = change in f(x) ÷ change in x between two rows.
b = f(x) − slope × x (or count back to x = 0).
Apply any shift (− 13) at the end.
tr: Reading the first row as the intercept when x ≠ 0
Forgetting the − 13 shift

tm.nm: Equation from a slope and a point in words
tl: “has a slope of 1/4 and passes through the point (0, 5)”
“parallel to line j”
tm.ask: the equation or a slope
tm.rl: y = mx + b; a point that is not (0, b) gives b = y − mx.
hd: m is the slope; b is the y-intercept (or y − mx from the point).
Parallel lines share the slope.
tr: Swapping slope and intercept

tm.nm: Read a linear graph: a value, an intercept, the slope, the equation
tl: a line drawn (often in context)
“y-intercept”, “at 60 rings”, “per second”, “which equation”, “graph of y = f(x) − 11”
tm.ask: a value, an intercept, the slope, the change, or the equation
tm.rl: Read lattice points; slope = rise ÷ run; undo any shift of the graph.
hd: Read the point(s) you need where the line crosses gridlines.
Slope = rise ÷ run; intercept where x = 0.
If the graph shows f(x) − 11, add 11 to its intercept for f.
Distance in the first 10 minutes = change in y, not y at 10.
tr: Forgetting to undo the shift (± 11)
Answering the final total instead of the change
Reading y = 2x − 5 as slope 1/2

tm.nm: Intercepts from the equation
tl: f(x) = mx + b given (maybe as a sum f + g or a shift g(x) − 2)
“x-intercept”, “y-intercept”, “a + b”
tm.ask: an intercept coordinate
tm.rl: y-intercept = f(0); x-intercept: solve f(x) = 0.
ds: Type the function; click the intercepts
hd: y-intercept: put x = 0.
x-intercept: set f(x) = 0 and solve.
Combine f + g first if h = f + g.
tr: Reporting the intercept of f instead of the shifted graph

tm.nm: What does this number mean?
tl: “best interpretation of 33 / the slope / s(3) = 121 / the x-intercept”
tm.ask: the meaning of a number, a value, or an intercept
tm.rl: Constant = value when x = 0 (or when x = h in a(x − h) form); coefficient = change per one unit of x; f(k) = v means input k gives output v.
hd: Name the input and output with units.
Constant: the output when the input is 0 (or h for x − h).
Coefficient: change in the output for each 1 of input; x-intercept: when the output reaches 0.
tr: Reading a(x − 3) as the value at x = 0
Swapping which quantity changes per which
Calling the constant a count of items

tm.nm: f(3x) given: find f(6)
tl: “f(3x) = x − 6 for all values of x”
tm.ask: a value of f, or the constant c
tm.rl: Choose x so the inside equals the input you need.
tr: Plugging 6 in for x directly

tm.nm: Output change = slope × input change
tl: a linear formula and “increased by 2.10”
tm.ask: the change in the output
tm.rl: Change in output = slope × change in input; the rest of the formula cancels.
tr: Evaluating F(2.10)

tm.nm: Write ax + by = c for a story
tl: two kinds of items, each with its own value per unit
a total
“which equation represents this situation”
tm.ask: the equation
tm.rl: Each value per unit goes with its own variable; the total is alone on the other side.
hd: Value of one x-item × x + value of one y-item × y = total.
Percents: (p/100)x + (q/100)y = total of the substance.
Perimeters: count × number of sides × side length.
tr: Pairing each value with the other variable
Adding the values (4(x + y))

tm.nm: Use the equation: plug in one value, solve for the other
tl: an equation like 2.5b + 5r = 80 (or a story giving one)
one of the two quantities given
tm.ask: the other quantity
tm.rl: Substitute the known value, then solve the one-variable equation.
hd: Put the given value in for its variable (convert units first if needed).
Solve for the other variable.
tr: Substituting into the wrong variable
Forgetting a unit change (minutes to hours)

tm.nm: Mixture equation px + qy = r(x + y)
tl: two solutions of given percents mixed to a third percent
the equation given
tm.ask: the amount of one solution
tm.rl: Substitute the known amount; solve.
tr: Decimal slips

tm.nm: Parallel and perpendicular slopes
tl: “line j is perpendicular (parallel) to line k”
k given as an equation (often ax + by = c) or a graph
tm.ask: the slope (or which pair stays perpendicular)
tm.rl: Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: negative reciprocal. From ax + by = c the slope is −a/b.
hd: Get line k’s slope: −a/b from standard form, rise/run from a graph.
Parallel: copy it. Perpendicular: flip and change the sign.
Perpendicular to a vertical line x = k: slope 0.
tr: Stopping at line k’s slope
Flipping without changing the sign
Using b/a instead of −a/b

tm.nm: Line through a point, parallel or perpendicular to another
tl: “passes through (0, 5) and is parallel to y = 7x + 4”
or a second point with an unknown coordinate
tm.ask: the equation or a coordinate
tm.rl: Same (or negative reciprocal) slope; the given point fixes the intercept.
hd: Slope from the given line (flip for perpendicular).
Intercept from the point; then substitute any other x.
tr: Keeping the old intercept

tm.nm: Meaning of a coefficient, term, constant or point in ax + by = c
tl: an equation like 3x + 5y = 32 in context
“best interpretation of 6 / 5y / 37 / the point (8, 10)”, “how many more … than …”
tm.ask: what a number or term means, or the difference of two per-unit values
tm.rl: Coefficient = value of one unit of its variable; term = total for that kind; constant = grand total.
hd: Coefficient: the amount for one item of that variable.
Term (5y): the total for all the y-items.
Difference of per-unit values: subtract the coefficients (45 − 5 = 40).
tr: Calling a term a count of items
Swapping which item a coefficient belongs to

tm.nm: Find the slope (from an equation, two points or intercepts)
tl: an equation not in y = mx + b form, two points, or two intercepts
“what is the slope”
tm.ask: the slope
tm.rl: Solve for y, or rise ÷ run; with intercepts (a, 0) and (0, b) the slope is −b/a.
ds: Type the equation; click two points on the line; rise/run
hd: Standard form: slope = −(x-coefficient)/(y-coefficient).
Two points: (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁).
Expand first if there are brackets.
tr: Sign error in −a/b
Run over rise

tm.nm: Find an intercept
tl: “the y-intercept is (0, y)”, “x-coordinate of the x-intercept”
an equation with fractions, or a graph
tm.ask: an intercept coordinate
tm.rl: y-intercept: set x = 0; x-intercept: set y = 0.
ds: Type the equation; click where the line crosses the axis
hd: Set the other variable to 0 and solve.
From slope and an x-intercept: b = −m·a.
tr: Setting the wrong variable to 0

tm.nm: Shift a line up or down: the new intercept
tl: “translated down 4 units”, “shifted down 5 units”
a standard-form equation or a table
tm.ask: an intercept of the shifted line
tm.rl: Shift down k: replace y with y + k (or subtract k from the y-intercept), then set y = 0 or x = 0.
ds: Type the original as y = …, then y = (…) − 4; click the new x-intercept
hd: Write the line as y = mx + b.
New intercept b − k; new x-intercept from 0 = mx + (b − k).
tr: Shifting the x-intercept left instead of moving the line down

tm.nm: Write the line’s equation from slope, points, a table or a graph
tl: a slope and a point, two points, a table, or a graph
“which equation defines/represents …”
choices with letter constants (R, s) or a shifted function f(x) + 14
tm.ask: the equation (or a constant in it)
tm.rl: Slope from two points, intercept from x = 0; with letters, match the intercepts of each choice.
ds: Table: x_1, y_1 then y_1~mx_1+b gives m and b at once
hd: Slope = rise ÷ run between two points.
Intercept: the y at x = 0 (or b = y − mx).
For a graph of f(x) + 14, subtract 14 from the intercept.
tr: Swapping slope and intercept
Forgetting to undo the + 14 shift
Sign of the constant in standard form

tm.nm: Which table fits the equation or graph?
tl: an equation or graph
choices are tables of three (x, y) pairs
tm.ask: the table
tm.rl: Test one row that differs between choices; Desmos table checks every row at once.
ds: Type the equation and add each table; the one whose points all lie on the line
hd: Plug the first x into the equation; keep tables whose first y matches.
Check a second row to break ties.
tr: Swapping x and y

tm.nm: A point with a missing coordinate on a line
tl: two points (table, graph or given), and a third point with a letter
“what is the value of a / d / k + n”
tm.ask: the missing coordinate (or constant)
tm.rl: Same slope between any two points; or find the equation and substitute.
ds: Table of the two points, y_1~mx_1+b, then evaluate at the given x
hd: Slope from the two known points.
Slope from a known point to the unknown one must match; solve.
tr: Using the slope upside down

tm.nm: Graph of combinations: an intercept is “all of one kind”
tl: a line of possible combinations of two items with a fixed total
“what is the value of s”, “approximate mass of one …”
tm.ask: a total, a unit value or a read-off
tm.rl: At the x-intercept everything is x-items: total = value per x-item × x-intercept.
hd: Read an intercept.
Total = intercept × value per unit (or value per unit = total ÷ intercept).
tr: Using the wrong axis’s intercept

tm.nm: Solve by substitution (one variable already isolated)
tl: “x = 2”, “y = 4x + 1”, or the second equation repeats the first one’s left side
“what is the value of …”
tm.ask: x, y, or a combination
tm.rl: Hand when a variable is alone; Desmos when the numbers are messy: graph both and click the intersection.
ds: y=4x+1 | 4y=15x-8 | click the intersection, then compute the asked combination
hd: Replace the isolated variable in the other equation.
Solve, then back-substitute.
Answer the combination asked (x − y, not x).
tr: Answering x when x − y or y is asked
Sign slip when substituting a negative

tm.nm: Add or subtract the equations to get the asked combination
tl: the question asks for x + y, 3x + 3y, 6(x − 2) …
coefficients that add or subtract to a multiple of the target
tm.ask: a combination of x and y
tm.rl: Add or subtract the equations first; the target usually appears in one step.
ds: Graph both, click the intersection, then compute the combination (slower but safe)
hd: Add (or subtract) the two equations.
Scale the result to the asked combination: 3x + 3y = −5.
tr: Solving for x and y separately (slow) and then mis-combining
Answering x − 2 instead of 6(x − 2)

tm.nm: Eliminate a variable
tl: both equations in standard form ax + by = c
“what is the value of x”
tm.ask: one variable
tm.rl: Add or subtract so one variable cancels; Desmos intersection for decimals.
ds: -x+y=-3.5 | x+3y=9.5 | click the intersection (5, 1.5)
hd: Scale one equation so a variable has opposite coefficients.
Add, solve, back-substitute if needed.
tr: Arithmetic slips with decimals

tm.nm: Read the solution from the graph
tl: two lines graphed
“what is the solution (x, y)”
Easy
tm.ask: the intersection point
tm.rl: The solution is where the lines cross.
hd: Find the crossing point on the grid and read both coordinates.
tr: Picking an intercept instead of the crossing

tm.nm: No solution: find the constant
tl: “h is a constant”
“the system has no solution”
almost all Hard
tm.ask: the constant (or a value it cannot be)
tm.rl: No solution = parallel lines: same slope (x/y coefficient ratio), different intercept.
ds: Slider for the constant: drag until the lines are parallel and separate
hd: Put both equations in the same form (ax + by = c).
Set the ratios of the x- and y-coefficients equal and solve for the constant.
Make sure the constants are not in the same ratio (otherwise the lines coincide).
tr: Solving for x and y
Choosing the value that makes the lines identical

tm.nm: Infinitely many solutions: find the constant(s)
tl: “infinitely many solutions”
one or two unknown constants, sometimes one line drawn
tm.ask: a constant, a sum or a ratio of constants
tm.rl: Same line: one equation is a multiple of the other, constants included.
ds: Graph the given line and type the second with sliders; drag until they coincide
hd: Find the factor that turns one equation into the other (28y ÷ 7y = 4).
Apply it to every term, including the constant.
With a graphed line, write its equation first.
tr: Matching the x-coefficients but not the constants

tm.nm: Which second equation gives no, one, or infinitely many solutions?
tl: “One of the two equations … is given”
“no solution / infinitely many / exactly one / at least one”
choices are equations (or I/II)
tm.ask: the equation that produces the stated count
tm.rl: Compare each choice with the given line: same slope + different intercept = none; same line = infinitely many; different slope = exactly one.
ds: Graph the given equation and each choice; look for parallel, identical, or crossing
hd: Rewrite the given equation as y = mx + b.
Rewrite each choice the same way and compare slopes and intercepts.
tr: Matching the slope when exactly one solution is asked
Missing that “at least one” includes infinitely many

tm.nm: How many solutions does this system have?
tl: a system (or four systems as choices)
“how many solutions”, “which system has no solution”, “how many points of intersection”
tm.ask: the number of solutions
tm.rl: Compare slopes and intercepts; a third line must pass through the existing crossing to keep a solution.
ds: Graph the equations; count crossings
hd: Scale one equation to compare with the other.
Same left side, different right side: zero; identical: infinitely many; else one.
tr: “Infinitely many” when the right sides differ
“Exactly two”

tm.nm: Two unknowns from two facts (story)
tl: two kinds of items, two prices or two percents
a total count and a total value, or “15 more than 3 times”
tm.ask: one of the unknowns (or an amount built from it)
tm.rl: Write two equations (count and value); solve with Desmos’ intersection or by elimination.
ds: x+y=11 | 4x+y=20 | click the intersection
hd: Name the two unknowns.
One equation for the count, one for the value (or the stated relationship).
Solve and answer the asked quantity (a cost, not a count, if asked).
tr: Answering the other unknown
Answering a count when the dollars spent are asked

tm.nm: Write the system for a story
tl: “which system of equations represents this situation”
two quantities, a total count and a total value
tm.ask: the system
tm.rl: Count equation adds the counts; value equation multiplies each count by its own rate.
hd: Count: f + r = total number.
Value: price × count for each, added, = total value.
Discounts: 25% off → 0.75m.
tr: Swapping the two totals
Pairing each rate with the other item
Using the discount instead of what is paid (0.25 for 0.75)

tm.nm: Match a system to its graph
tl: graphs as choices, or a graph and equations as choices
“which system is represented”, “has the same solution”
tm.ask: the matching graph or system
tm.rl: Use intercepts: set x = 0 and y = 0 in each equation.
ds: Type the choice’s equations; compare with the picture
hd: Find each line’s intercepts from the equations.
Match to the graph (or check the graph’s crossing point in each choice).
tr: Matching only one of the two lines

tm.nm: Same line twice: points in terms of r
tl: two equations that are multiples of each other
“for each real number r, which point lies on both graphs”
tm.ask: a point in terms of r
tm.rl: Both equations are the same line; substitute each choice into one of them.
hd: Substitute the choice’s coordinates into 2x + 3y = 7; the one that simplifies to 7 for every r wins.
tr: Solving for y and stopping at the wrong form

tm.nm: Lines meet at (4, y): find a constant
tl: constants a and b in both equations
“intersect at the point (4, y)”
tm.ask: a constant
tm.rl: Substitute x = 4 into both, eliminate the shared unknown.
hd: Put x = 4 in both equations.
Combine so b and y drop out together (by appears in both), then solve for a.

tm.nm: Which point or table satisfies the inequality (or system)?
tl: an inequality or a system, or a shaded graph
choices are ordered pairs, tables of (x, y) values, regions or Roman-numeral lists
“which … is a solution”, “all … solutions”
tm.ask: the point, table or region that satisfies every inequality
tm.rl: Desmos: type the inequalities and see which points land in the overlap; by hand, substitute and watch the boundary (< versus ≤).
ds: y<6x+2 (and the other inequality) | add a table of the choice’s points, or type (14,0) | the point must sit inside every shading
hd: Substitute each point (or each row of a table) into every inequality.
Strict < fails on the boundary itself.
For tables, one failing row kills the choice.
tr: A table whose row lands exactly on the boundary of a strict inequality
A point that satisfies only one inequality of the system
A point on the right side of a steep line but outside the shading

tm.nm: Which inequality does the shading show?
tl: a shaded half-plane with a solid or dashed line
“represents the solutions to which inequality”, or a constant inside the inequality
tm.ask: the inequality (or its constant)
tm.rl: Line from two grid points; shading above = y >, below = y <; dashed = strict.
ds: Type each choice and compare its shading with the picture
hd: Read the boundary line’s intercept and slope.
Above the line: y > …; below: y < …; dashed means no “or equal”.
If a coefficient multiplies y, dividing by a negative flips the sign.
tr: Swapping x and y for a horizontal or vertical line
Ignoring the flip when dividing by a negative constant

tm.nm: Greatest or least whole number allowed
